messages:
Evan: hey team, quick intro — I'm Evan, started today in platform eng. Trying to get kubectl access to the ci-cd namespace but `kubectl get pods -n ci-cd` returns Forbidden. Who should I ping for kubeconfig/roles?
Sylvia (eng-infra): welcome Evan :wave: pinging eng-infra. Can you paste the output of `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n ci-cd`?
Evan: current-context is `rwd-dev-us-west-2`, `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n ci-cd` -> "no". Also my email is evan@redwood.com and my SSO username is `evan.l`
eng-infra-bot: Created access ticket INFRA-2318 for Evan (evan.l). Assignee: Sylvia. ETA: ~15m.
Sylvia (eng-infra): thanks. I granted a RoleBinding to the `developers` group and created a serviceaccount `evan-sa` in `ci-cd`. To use it locally you can exec a token like this:```bash
kubectl -n ci-cd create token evan-sa --duration=24h
# then set a user with that token
kubectl config set-credentials evan-sa --token=<PASTE_TOKEN>
kubectl config set-context evan-ci-cd --cluster=rwd-dev-cluster --namespace=ci-cd --user=evan-sa
kubectl config use-context evan-ci-cd
```
Evan: nice — running the first command now...
Evan: ok got a token, set the creds and switched context, `kubectl get pods -n ci-cd` now shows pods. Thanks!! :tada:
Todd: quick security note — service account tokens are scoped; for any long-running automation prefer a short-lived kubeconfig or OIDC flow. If you need admin-like perms for a demo ask and we'll do a temp grant + audit log.
Priyanka: also FYI if you use the `rwd-dev` context in multiple terminals, consider `kubectl config rename-context` or export `KUBECONFIG` per shell to avoid accidents.
Ben (oncall): adding that the oncall runbook for ci-cd is in #eng-sre under docs/ci-cd/k8s. If you see an incident ping @oncall.
Evan: appreciated everyone, access verified and noticed one pod in CrashLoopBackOff — will open a separate thread for debugging. Thanks for the help and the warm welcome :smile:
Sylvia (eng-infra): welcome aboard Evan! If anything else pops up DM me or drop in #eng-infra.
